2027-02-24.title: Wednesday of the Second Week of Lent
readings: Come, let us make plots against Jeremiah
Save me, O Lord, in your steadfast love
They will condemn him to death
2027-02-24.alt: Lenten weekday. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-24.verse: just as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.”
theo: Jeremiah has spoken God's word faithfully, and now the people plot against him. They say: let us bring charges against him and not heed any of his words. The prophet turns to God in pain: “Is evil a recompense for good? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good for them, to turn away your wrath from them.” He had prayed for the very people who now want him dead. Jeremiah is a figure of Christ, the innocent one who intercedes for those who reject him. The Psalm puts the words of trust on our lips that Jesus himself prayed on the cross: “Into your hand I commit my spirit; you have redeemed me, O LORD, faithful God.” And again: “My times are in your hand.”

In the Gospel Jesus, going up to Jerusalem, tells the Twelve for the third time what awaits him: he will be handed over, condemned, mocked, flogged and crucified, “and on the third day he will be raised.” At that very moment the mother of James and John kneels before him and asks for the best places in his kingdom. Jesus answers gently: “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?” They say, “We are able,” not knowing that the cup is suffering. And the other ten are angry, perhaps because they wanted the same places. So Jesus teaches them all: among the nations rulers lord it over others, “It will not be so among you; but whoever wishes to be great among you must be your servant.” Then he gives the reason, the heart of the whole Gospel: “the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.” In Lent we follow him up to Jerusalem. The question is not which seat we will have, but whether we will drink his cup with him.
outline: Ask: if you could ask Jesus for one honour, what would it be?
Jeremiah, the prophet who prayed for his enemies.
Point 2 · Can you drink the cup?
Point 3 · Not to be served but to serve
“The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve.”
live: Serve, do not seek to be served (Matthew 20:28)
Take the lowest task at home or at work today without comment.
Pray for those who hurt you
Like Jeremiah, speak good of someone before God who has spoken ill of you.
2027-02-24.prayer: Lord Jesus, you went up to Jerusalem to give your life as a ransom for many. Free us from the desire for the first places, teach us to drink your cup with trust, and make us servants of all. Into your hands we commit our spirit. Amen.
altar: The cup that Jesus asked the disciples to drink is the cup he offers us at every Mass: the cup of his Blood, poured out for many. To receive it is to share his self-giving love.

quick: Jeremiah was repaid with evil for the good he did, and still prayed.
James and John asked for honours; Jesus offered them his cup.
The Son of Man came to serve and to give his life as a ransom.
2027-02-24.action: Take the last place or the hardest task today, quietly.
2027-02-24.question: Where am I still seeking the first place, even in my faith or my service?

family.explain: Two of Jesus' friends wanted to be the most important. Jesus said: the most important one is the one who serves everyone. Jesus came to serve us and even gave his life for us.
family.intention: We pray for people who serve others quietly: cleaners, nurses, cooks, drivers.
family.ask: Ask: “Who serves our family every day? How can we thank them?”

illus: At a parish feast in Thrissur, the committee members were arguing about who would sit on the stage with the bishop. Meanwhile an elderly man nobody knew was washing the plates behind the hall. When the bishop arrived, he went to the kitchen first, greeted the old man, and took a towel. The committee members quietly followed him.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you came not to be served but to serve. Give us your humble heart. Amen.
share: Is evil a recompense for good? (Jeremiah 18:20). How do I respond when I am repaid with ingratitude?
Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink? (Matthew 20:22). What cup is Jesus offering me?
Whoever wishes to be great among you must be your servant (Matthew 20:26). Whom am I called to serve?
pm.resp: Save me, O Lord, in your steadfast love.
interc: For those who are persecuted for speaking the truth.
For leaders in Church and society, that they may serve and not dominate.
For those who serve in hidden ways, that God may reward them.
For mothers who pray for their children's future.
For our group, that we may follow Jesus to Jerusalem.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave his life as a ransom for many. Make us servants after his heart. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Jeremiah had prayed for his people, and they plotted to kill him. He cried to God: is evil a recompense for good? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good for them (Jeremiah 18:20). He is a picture of Jesus, who prayed for those who crucified him.

In the Gospel Jesus tells the Twelve for the third time that he will be condemned and crucified and raised on the third day. And at that very moment the mother of James and John asks for the best seats for her sons. We do the same: we bring Jesus our ambitions while he is speaking of the cross.

Jesus answers: you do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink? (Matthew 20:22). The cup is his suffering. Later, James would be the first of the apostles to die as a martyr. He did drink the cup.

Then Jesus teaches all of us: it will not be so among you; whoever wishes to be great among you must be your servant… just as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many (Matthew 20:26–28). This Lent, let us stop asking for seats and start taking up towels. Amen.
kids: Children, two friends of Jesus wanted to be the most important. Jesus said: the most important person is the one who helps everyone. Jesus came to help us and to give his life for us. Today, help someone at home without being asked!

intro: Theme: “Not to be served but to serve.”
The persecuted prophet, the cup of the Lord and the greatness of service.

sub: A prophet who prayed for his enemies.
q: Is evil a recompense for good? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good for them, to turn away your wrath from them.
Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing.”
points.apply: Pray by name for someone who has repaid your good with evil.

points.apply: Accept one difficulty today as a sip from the Lord's cup, and offer it with trust.

points.h: Not to be served but to serve

The way to greatness in the kingdom is the towel and the cup.
